report.answer_text:
Hakainde Hichilema is the president of Zambia. He was first elected in August 2021.[1] He won re-election for a second five-year term[2] in the August 2026 election. Election commission results gave him roughly 61.4 percent of valid votes, against 38 percent for his main challenger, Brian Mundubile.[2] The election was marred by allegations of fraud.[2]
He was sworn in for his second term on 1 September 2026.[3] His running mate, Mutale Nalumango, was sworn in as vice-president at the same ceremony.[3]
